text:
B: Alright mate, how's it going?
A: Alright, yeah. Can you hear me okay?
B: Yeah, loud and clear. I'm Lewis.
A: Luke. Nice one.
B: Saw your photo. Southampton, yeah? With the team picture.
A: Yeah, that's me. My dad's fault, to be fair. You're Spurs, I saw the shirt.
B: Guilty. Don't start, I know. We bottle it every year, it's tradition at this point.
A: I wasn't gonna say anything. We've got no room to talk, mate.
B: Ha, fair. So what d'you do then?
A: Erm, I'm a shift manager at a parcel depot. In Basingstoke. Early shift, so about forty people, sorters and loaders.
B: Early shift, what's that, like five?
A: I'm in for half five. So I'm sort of knackered by about Wednesday. By Friday I'm basically a zombie.
B: Rather you than me, mate. I'd be useless.
A: What about you?
B: I've got my own business, tiling. Bathrooms, kitchen floors, that kind of thing. Bishop's Stortford, round Harlow. Bit of everything really. Plan is to get a couple of lads under me, do full bathroom fits, get the name on the van, you know.
A: Oh, nice. Is it busy?
B: Yeah, it's alright. Comes and goes. Mostly word of mouth, through my dad's mates and a builder I know. Don't really need to advertise, to be fair.
A: That's handy. Word of mouth's the best way, isn't it.
B: Yeah, and you can sort of pick your hours. I don't do Wednesday nights, that's five-a-side.
A: I used to play. Stopped after my knee went a bit. Not properly went, just sort of twinged and I thought, yeah, I'm done.
B: Knees, mate. Don't. Kneeling on floors all day, I reckon mine are gonna be shot by forty.
A: Yeah, that can't be good for you long term, can it.
B: Nah. So what else, you do anything at the weekends?
A: Fishing, mostly. Carp. There's a couple of lakes near me, I go down on a Saturday and sit there all day. Caught a decent common last weekend actually, about eighteen pound. Bit quiet for most people, but it's sort of the only time I'm not thinking about work.
B: Eighteen pound? That's a big fish. Do you eat 'em?
A: No, no, you put 'em back. Photo, back in. That's the whole thing.
B: Mad. Sit there all day and then let it go. I'd get bored, I'm not gonna lie.
A: Everyone says that. My girlfriend thinks I'm mental. But it's peaceful, you know. No one ringing me about a missing cage.
B: Ha. Yeah, see, that's why I like being my own boss. Nobody ringing me. Well, clients, but I just don't answer sometimes.
A: Bet they love that.
B: They get over it. Do you play FC, the PlayStation one?
A: Yeah, online with a couple of mates. I'm rubbish though, to be fair.
B: We should get a game in, mate, I'll stick you on—
